# Example files

## Overview

`ems_example()` writes bundled example model and script files to disk.
It is a good starting point for new users, providing ready-to-run material for each of the six vetted models without requiring any additional setup beyond GTAP data access.

Two output modes are available, controlled by the `type` argument:

- `"model_files"` (default): writes the model (`.tab`) and closure (`.cls`) files for the chosen model.
- `"scripts"`: writes a complete set of example R scripts covering a range of shock, swap, and solver configurations supported by that model.
  Each script is a self-contained, runnable workflow from data loading through to result parsing.

```r
ems_example(
  model,
  path,
  type = c("model_files", "scripts"),
  dat_input = NULL,
  par_input = NULL,
  set_input = NULL
)
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `model` | | Model name. One of `"GTAPv6"`, `"GTAPv7"`, `"GTAP-RE"`, `"GTAP-AEZ"`, `"GTAP-E"`, `"GTAP-EP"`, `"ORANI-G"` |
| `path` | | Directory where files will be written |
| `type` | `"model_files"` | Output type: `"model_files"` or `"scripts"` |
| `dat_input` | `NULL` | Path to the basedata HAR file, or the `dat` list from [`GTAP_convert()`](data_load.qmd). Required when `type = "scripts"` |
| `par_input` | `NULL` | Path to the parameters HAR file, or the `par` list from [`GTAP_convert()`](data_load.qmd). Required when `type = "scripts"` for a GTAP model |
| `set_input` | `NULL` | Path to the sets HAR file, or the `set` list from [`GTAP_convert()`](data_load.qmd). Required when `type = "scripts"` for a GTAP model |

## Writing model files

The simplest use of `ems_example()` extracts a model's Tablo and closure files so they can be inspected or used directly with [`ems_model()`](model_load.qmd) or [`solve_in_situ()`](solve.qmd).

```r
library(teems)

# Write GTAPv7 model files to a temporary directory
paths <- ems_example("GTAPv7", tempdir())

# Or to a specific directory
paths <- ems_example("GTAP-RE", "~/my_project/model")
```

The returned list contains two named paths:

```r
paths[["model_file"]]   # path to the .tab file
paths[["closure_file"]] # path to the .cls file
```

These can be passed directly to [`ems_model()`](model_load.qmd):

```r
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = paths[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = paths[["closure_file"]]
)
```

## Writing example scripts

When `type = "scripts"`, `ems_example()` writes a directory of R scripts covering a range of configurations available for the chosen model.
Each script is injected with the supplied data paths and is immediately runnable.

```r
paths <- ems_example(
  model = "GTAPv7",
  path = "~/my_project",
  type = "scripts",
  dat_input = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/flexAgg/gsdfdat.har",
  par_input = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/flexAgg/gsdfpar.har",
  set_input = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/flexAgg/gsdfset.har"
)
```

The GTAP-AEZ scripts need a GTAP-AEZ database (GTAP 11c or newer).
The scripts pass the HAR files to `ems_data()`, which prepares the AEZ layer on load; `GTAP_convert(target = "GTAP-AEZ")` gives the prepared, unaggregated database in R (see [GTAP-AEZ, GTAP-E and GTAP-Power databases](data_load.qmd#gtap-aez-gtap-e-and-gtap-power-databases)):

```r
paths <- ems_example(
  model = "GTAP-AEZ",
  path = "~/my_project",
  type = "scripts",
  dat_input = "~/dat/GTAP-AEZ/v12a/gsdfdat.har",
  par_input = "~/dat/GTAP-AEZ/v12a/gsdfpar.har",
  set_input = "~/dat/GTAP-AEZ/v12a/gsdfset.har"
)
```

The GTAP-E scripts need a GTAP-E database (GTAP 12a or newer), prepared by `ems_data()` on load or with `GTAP_convert(target = "GTAP-E")` (see [GTAP-AEZ, GTAP-E and GTAP-Power databases](data_load.qmd#gtap-aez-gtap-e-and-gtap-power-databases)).
They aggregate with the `energy` mapping, which keeps the energy commodities distinct as the model's nest requires:

```r
paths <- ems_example(
  model = "GTAP-E",
  path = "~/my_project",
  type = "scripts",
  dat_input = "~/dat/GTAP-E/12a/gsdfdat.har",
  par_input = "~/dat/GTAP-E/12a/gsdfpar.har",
  set_input = "~/dat/GTAP-E/12a/gsdfset.har"
)
```

The GTAP-EP scripts need a GTAP-Power database (GTAP 12a or newer), prepared by `ems_data()` on load or with `GTAP_convert(target = "GTAP-EP")` (see [GTAP-AEZ, GTAP-E and GTAP-Power databases](data_load.qmd#gtap-aez-gtap-e-and-gtap-power-databases)).
They aggregate with the `power` mapping, which keeps transmission, base load and peak load apart as the generation nest requires:

```r
paths <- ems_example(
  model = "GTAP-EP",
  path = "~/my_project",
  type = "scripts",
  dat_input = "~/dat/GTAP-P/12a/gsdfdat.har",
  par_input = "~/dat/GTAP-P/12a/gsdfpar.har",
  set_input = "~/dat/GTAP-P/12a/gsdfset.har"
)
```

The ORANI-G scripts need only the model's own `basedata.har`, loaded through the single-file route of `ems_data()` (see [Loading data](data_load.qmd#input-files)).
`ems_example()` returns the short-run closure and writes the long-run closure `ORANI-G-LR.cls` beside it, which the `longrun` script loads:

```r
paths <- ems_example(
  model = "ORANI-G",
  path = "~/my_project",
  type = "scripts",
  dat_input = "~/dat/ORANI-G/basedata.har"
)
```

The data inputs can also be the in-memory list objects returned by [`GTAP_convert()`](data_load.qmd), which is useful when the raw data needs format conversion before running:

```r
# Convert v7.1 data to v6.2 format, then generate scripts for the classic model
converted <- GTAP_convert(
  dat_har = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/gsdfdat.har",
  par_har = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/gsdfpar.har",
  set_har = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/gsdfset.har",
  target = "GTAPv6"
)

paths <- ems_example(
  model = "GTAPv6",
  path = "~/my_project",
  type = "scripts",
  dat_input = converted$dat,
  par_input = converted$par,
  set_input = converted$set
)
```

When list objects are supplied, `ems_example()` writes data to RDS files alongside the scripts and injects `readRDS()` calls at the top of each script in place of plain path assignments.

## Using the generated scripts

`ems_example()` returns a character vector of paths, one per written script.
Each script is ready to run; the data paths supplied to `ems_example()` are injected at the top of the file as plain assignments.

### Script naming convention

Script file names encode the shock and swap configuration (the exact set varies by model):

| File name | What it demonstrates |
|-----------|----------------------|
| `null.R` | Zero-shock run — useful for verifying the model solves before applying shocks |
| `numeraire.R` | Uniform shock to the numeraire (`pfactwld`): all prices move by the shock and real variables stay unchanged |
| `full_uniform.R` | Uniform shock across all elements of a variable |
| `part_uniform.R` | Uniform shock on a subset of elements |
| `part_uniform_full_swap.R` | Partial shock plus a full-variable closure swap |
| `part_uniform_part_swap.R` | Partial shock plus a partial closure swap |
| `part_uniform_part_swap_mixed.R` | Partial shock plus mixed (full + partial) swaps |
| `part_uniform_subset_swap.R` | Partial shock and swaps with mixed multiple elements and subsets |
| `custom_full.R` | Heterogeneous shock values supplied as a data frame |
| `custom_partial.R` | Heterogeneous shock values supplied as a data frame on a subset of elements |
| `custom_full_csv.R` | Heterogeneous shock values read from a CSV file |
| `custom_partial_*.R` | Heterogeneous shocks with one or more dimensions fixed to elements |
| `*_year.R`, `scenario.R` | Intertemporal models only: shocks by chronological year, and a [scenario shock](scenario_shocks.qmd) |

### Structure of a generated script

Each script begins with the injected assignments followed by the template body.
Opening `part_uniform.R` in an editor shows:

```r
dat_input = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/flexAgg/gsdfdat.har"
par_input = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/flexAgg/gsdfpar.har"
set_input = "~/dat/GTAP/v12/flexAgg/gsdfset.har"
model_file = "~/my_project/GTAP-RE.tab"
closure_file = "~/my_project/GTAP-RE.cls"

dat <- ems_data(
  dat_input = dat_input,
  par_input = par_input,
  set_input = set_input,
  time_steps = c(0, 1, 2),
  REG = "big3",
  ACTS = "macro_sector",
  ENDW = "labor_agg"
)

model <- ems_model(
  model_file = model_file,
  closure_file = closure_file
)

partial <- ems_uniform_shock(
  var = "aoall",
  value = -1,
  REGr = "chn",
  ACTSa = "crops"
)

cmf_path <- ems_deploy(
  .data = dat,
  model = model,
  shock = partial
)

outputs <- ems_solve(
  cmf_path = cmf_path,
  matrix_method = "SBBD",
  n_tasks = 2L,
  solution_method = "Gragg"
)
```

## Output

`ems_example()` returns a character vector of file paths to the written files.
For `type = "model_files"` this is the `.tab` and `.cls` paths.
For `type = "scripts"` this is one path per written script.
